evidence.statement: QatarEnergy restored LNG exports in September to about a third of pre-war levels, and at least 20 more cargoes have passed Hormuz since early September (Semafor, citing Bloomberg).

Much of Ras Laffan has been shut since the war began; Kpler put September LNG exports at 1.6 million tonnes, under a quarter of the pre-war average, with October on track for 0.6 million tonnes (Reuters, via Cyprus Mail).
Wood Mackenzie expected the North site back within a month of a restart; the strikes that damaged two trains hit the South site (The National).
QatarEnergy declared force majeure on its entire LNG output after missile and rocket attacks on Ras Laffan caused fires and extensive damage (Fox Business, citing Reuters).
